fatal_errors: The proposed reactive SPS route does not reconstruct the target liquid-metal dealloying method using molten Cu at 1200 °C for 96 h.
It omits the directionally segregated WTaVTi precursor and preferential replacement of Ti/V-rich interdendritic channels by Cu.

Its mechanism of suppressing diffusion and locking in a homogeneous powder microstructure conflicts with the target mechanism of selective Ti dissolution, Cu ingress, and formation of a W-rich passivating interlayer.

The cited evidence reports SPS consolidation of a Cu-free NbMoTaWVTi alloy and provides no support for RHEA–Cu compatibility, in situ synchrotron control, large-scale reaction, irradiation resistance, or thermal transport.
In situ XRD is principally diagnostic and cannot itself improve the product unless a specified feedback-controlled processing intervention changes the SPS schedule.
explanation: The hypothesis recognizes the broad challenge of producing a stable RHEA–Cu composite, but otherwise diverges from the demonstrated approach. The target used liquid-metal dealloying to exploit precursor segregation: molten Cu selectively replaced Ti-rich interdendritic material while continuous refractory ligaments and an approximately 300 nm W-rich interlayer stabilized the bicontinuous interface. None of these defining materials, conditions, structures, or mechanisms appears in the proposal. Its outcomes are generic and omit the measured thermal-conductivity increase and qualified He-irradiation comparison. The proposed falsification test is also weak because samples cannot simultaneously have identical processing conditions and differ through monitoring-guided optimization; passive XRD monitoring should not alter properties. A defensible test would compare fixed versus feedback-adjusted SPS schedules and directly measure Cu segregation, interfacial reactions, thermal conductivity, and irradiation response. E1 supports only that an RHEA can be synthesized by MA/SPS, not the central RHEA–Cu or synchrotron-guidance claims.
